subject: Human Body
title: Skin and the Immune System
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Skin and the Immune System.

hook.text: Your skin isn't just a wall. It's patrolled by immune cells that detect and fight invaders that breach the surface.

buildup.text: Langerhans cells in the epidermis capture foreign antigens and present them to T cells, triggering immune responses.

discovery.text: Skin also produces antimicrobial peptides called defensins.

twist.text: Tattoo ink persists because macrophages eat it, die, and release it for new macrophages to eat.

climax.text: Skin is an active immune organ.

punchline.text: Tattoos survive because immune cells eat the ink forever.

quiz.question: Why does tattoo ink stay in the skin permanently?
options: Ink bonds chemically with collagen fibers
Macrophages eat the ink, die, and pass it to new macrophages endlessly
The epidermis seals the ink below its layers during healing
